message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm player 2 with $975 and hotels on the dark blues and reds. The opponent has $293 and hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic. I just paid $70 rent to them. I have a lot of cash but only one opponent left.

I'm calculating whether the opponent can survive my hotel rent. Boardwalk and Park Place hotels each cost $2000 and $1500. Illinois, Indiana, and Kentucky hotels each cost $1100 and $1050. I also noted many of their properties are mortgaged.

I mapped the board positions. The opponent is on North Carolina Avenue.

The opponent can land on Park Place or Boardwalk this turn. Both hotels cost over $1,500. With only $293 cash, they cannot pay the rent and will likely go bankrupt.

I'm calculating the opponent's liquid assets. Their brown hotels are worth roughly $250 total, or about $125 each. I also noted their utilities and brown deeds add to their available cash.

The $70 difference in the opponent's cash is the rent I just paid them. Their full liquidation is roughly $543, combining $293 cash with the $250 from brown hotels.

I realized mortgaged properties cannot be sold back to the bank for cash. The opponent's brown hotels are their only liquid assets. They must sell buildings before mortgaging any brown properties.

The opponent's total liquid assets are roughly $753. Even after collecting $200 from passing GO, they still cannot afford the hotel rent on Park Place or Boardwalk. I am now weighing whether to unmortgage any of my own properties.

I checked the unmortgage costs for my remaining properties. Unmortgaging the light blues would not give me a monopoly, since the opponent owns Oriental. The orange group is fully mortgaged and complete, but I do not own all three spaces yet. I also noted the pink properties are split between us.

I now own all three orange properties, but they are fully mortgaged. The pink, light blue, and yellow groups remain split between us. The greens are split as well; I own Pennsylvania Avenue while the opponent owns Pacific and North Carolina.

Unmortgaging all three orange properties would cost $616. After doing so, I would have only $359 left. Building one house on each property costs $300, leaving just $59. The resulting rent is only $50 to $60 per turn, which is far below the opponent's cash. Two houses are impossible with this budget.

Unmortgaging New York alone would cost $220 and yield only $16 in rent, so it is not worth it.

The opponent on North Carolina has a roughly 28% chance of rolling a 5 or 7 this turn and landing on Park Place or Boardwalk. A roll of 6 would land them on luxury tax for $75, which they can afford. Any roll of 8 or higher would let them pass GO safely.

Rolls of 1 through 4 are safe. The opponent could survive to pass GO and collect $200, raising their cash to roughly $493 or $418 after luxury tax. Even then they would still die to my dark blue and red hotels on the next lap. I am weighing whether unmortgaging the orange properties will speed up victory or risk depleting my cash cushion. I am also checking what happens if I land on their mortgaged St. Charles Avenue.

I cannot land on the opponent's unmortgaged hotels this turn. From Electric Company, reaching their hotels on Baltic, Mediterranean, or Water Works requires moving 16 to 31 spaces, which exceeds the maximum roll of 12.

I cannot land on their hotels or utilities this turn. The maximum I can reach is Illinois, which is mine. A chance card could send me to Boardwalk or Reading, but luxury tax and income tax are also unreachable from here.

I should not unmortgage the orange properties. That would burn my cash cushion, and my dark blue and red hotels already kill the opponent. I must also avoid trading away any property that would complete a monopoly for them. Selling Pennsylvania Avenue would let them finish their greens. Selling States Avenue would let them finish their pinks. Selling Vermont or Connecticut would let them finish their light blue group. Any trade that gives them a completed monopoly could backfire if they build houses and land on those spaces before they die.

Selling hotels would weaken my kill zones. I should end the turn. Unmortgaging cheap properties for passive rent is unnecessary because the opponent cannot skip my red and dark blue hotels on their next lap. They already passed the Go to Jail space, so they cannot avoid those high-rent squares.

The opponent will hit the red hotels before reaching Go to Jail on their next lap. A roll of 4 this turn could land them on Chance space 36, which might send them to jail or Boardwalk. Even if they avoid the reds for a turn, they must eventually leave jail and still face the board.

The opponent cannot survive any hotel landing. Their maximum liquid assets are roughly $753, while my red and dark blue hotels each cost over $1,000. They must pass through the red stretch of three consecutive spaces and the dark blue group of two, so missing all three hotel squares is statistically unlikely.
